## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Indriyakathā* ("Discourse on the Controlling Powers" or "Faculties") is the eighth text of the nineteenth chapter of the *Kathāvatthu*, situated within the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [Catalog; Hazra 1994]. SuttaCentral records one modern translation in one language [SuttaCentral].

The text addresses a doctrinal controversy regarding whether spiritual qualities such as confidence (*saddhā*), energy (*viriya*), mindfulness (*sati*), concentration (*samādhi*), and wisdom (*paññā*) can properly be distinguished from their status as "faculties" (*indriya*, such as *saddhindriya*) on the premise that ordinary (*lokiya*) qualities are merely mundane mental factors while the faculties are exclusively supramundane or transcendent (*lokuttara*) [Gethin 2001]. The *Kathāvatthu* rejects this restriction, asserting that it is entirely legitimate to designate mundane confidence and the other four qualities as faculties [Gethin 2001]. According to the *Kathāvatthu* commentary cited by modern scholars, this opposing thesis was upheld by the Hetuvādins and the Mahīśāsakas [Gethin 2001].

Regarding textual connections, SuttaCentral records mentions and thematic relationships with several discourses and texts, including the *Mahāpadāna Sutta* (DN 14), *Pāsarāsi Sutta* (MN 26), *Bodhirājakumāra Sutta* (MN 85), *Brahmāyācanasutta* (SN 6.1), sections of the *Cūḷaniddesa* and *Mahāniddesa*, and parallel passages in Sanskrit literature such as the *Mahāvastu* and *Saṅghabhedavastu* [SuttaCentral]. The DharmaNexus text-reuse matches with MN 26, MN 85, and the *Niddesa* treatises confirm the thematic links identified by SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
